title: Logistics Route Optimization via Hadoop
business: Global logistics firms managing millions of daily sensor events from shipping containers.
problem: Traditional relational databases fail to ingest and process massive, high-velocity telemetry streams, leading to delayed route adjustments and increased fuel costs.
solution: Hadoop provides a distributed framework where HDFS stores raw sensor data across commodity hardware, while YARN manages resource allocation for MapReduce jobs that calculate optimal paths in parallel.
steps: Deploy HDFS across a cluster to provide high-throughput access to raw sensor telemetry files.
Configure YARN to manage cluster resources, ensuring compute tasks do not starve each other.
Develop MapReduce jobs to parse and aggregate container location data into regional summaries.
Execute parallel processing tasks to identify route inefficiencies based on historical transit times.
Store processed results back into HDFS for downstream reporting and logistics planning.
outcome: The organization achieves the ability to process vast volumes of historical sensor data to identify systemic transit delays without requiring expensive, proprietary hardware upgrades.
limitation: The system introduces significant latency for real-time decision-making because MapReduce is designed for batch processing; check this by monitoring job completion times in the YARN resource manager dashboard.
